source_review.notes: Checked all six current official/standards sources. The September 2025 specification supports validation, field collection, execution, introspection, and response/error mechanics. Current GraphQL Foundation authorization guidance places policy in the business logic layer; security guidance covers depth, breadth, aliases, batching, pagination, rate limits, demand control, and trusted documents; performance guidance supports batching/caching/pagination evidence. Current OWASP GraphQL and Authorization cheat sheets support input/resource bounds, cost/rate/time controls, BOLA/BFLA protection, deny-default/least privilege, correct enforcement placement, error redaction, and testing.

evidence: Checked actor a, action x, resource r, context c, policy p, decision A, normalized operation O, nodes V, weights w_v, multipliers m_v, children ch(v), budgets B_s/B_r, quota Q, observed work W, and document record D for consistent domains.
Confirmed Boolean authorization, recursive cost, vector budget, set/range, and partial-order notation matches prose.
Confirmed authentication, authorization, decision granularity, PEP/PDP, deny-default, static/runtime cost, trusted document, and semantic rate limiting are defined.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation keeps authorization truth independent from estimated cost, observed work, quotas, and document lifecycle.

evidence: Executed the teaching cost model: cheap tree cost 3 and nested list tree cost 1+5*(1+(1+10*1))=61 against budget 50, yielding true then false admission.
Recomputed Exercise 2: price 2; items 2+10*2=22; per-order children 23; orders 3+20*23=463; root 2+463=465.
Checked the 50-by-100 example represents up to 5,000 member positions before leaf/dependency additions.
Counted ten examples and five exercise-answer pairs.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Numbers are exact model examples, not measured production costs or recommended universal thresholds.

evidence: Constructed cross-tenant same-ID actors proving possession/opacity cannot imply authorization.
Constructed visible-parent/confidential-child case proving parent authorization does not generally imply relationship or field authorization.
Constructed shallow n-alias operations and nested m-by-m lists proving depth and breadth gates independently incomplete.
Confirmed fixed trusted text cannot imply current actor-resource permission or unchanged resolver cost.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: Implications and counterexamples remain scoped to explicit policy, normalized operation, and implementation-cost assumptions.

evidence: Reviewed anonymous/authenticated/delegated actors; absent/forbidden/cross-tenant/type-confused resources; direct, nested, node, search, edge, payload, subscription, federation, batch, cache, and background reachability.
Reviewed deep, wide, aliased, fragmented, list-multiplied, abstract, introspection, invalid, multi-operation, HTTP-batched, incremental, defaulted/variable operations and sensitive-action repetition.

Reviewed cache/PDP failure, policy change, manifest rollout/revocation, estimator underpricing, timeout/cancellation, quota distribution, gateway bypass, timing/count/error/log leakage, and instance exhaustion.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Coverage spans authorization completeness, parser/validator demand, execution resources, federation, lifecycle, side channels, and abuse.

evidence: The graphql-static-cost program checks nonnegative recursive weights, nested cardinality multiplication, and budget comparison.
Confirmed every disclosure/effect path reaches actor-action-resource policy and loaders/caches preserve visibility context.
Confirmed admission precedes resolver/transaction work and runtime deadline/call/row/byte/CPU/concurrency limits remain active.
Confirmed trusted documents bind exact text/client/environment/schema/lifecycle without bypassing authorization, variables, quotas, or runtime controls.
invariant_checking.notes: The executable model demonstrates arithmetic only; policy engines, schema normalization, dependencies, quotas, and containment require integration evidence.

evidence: Reviewed ID-possession counterexample and confirmed it separates lookup from permission.
Reviewed parent-child counterexample and confirmed it requires independent policy unless a domain invariant proves equivalent visibility.
Reviewed structural-limit counterexamples and confirmed depth, breadth, and list multiplication are complementary.
Reviewed static-versus-runtime argument and confirmed variable data/cache/dependency/retry state refutes runtime guarantee.
Reviewed trusted-document argument and confirmed fixed text cannot prove authorization or future cost.
proof_review.notes: Proof arguments are valid and explicitly avoid treating any single control as sufficient.

evidence: Confirmed GraphQL-specified behavior, Foundation guidance, OWASP recommendations, domain policy, static model, and runtime evidence are separated.
Confirmed authentication, authorization, admission, quota, trusted text, introspection restriction, and containment are independent controls.
Confirmed cost weights are labeled estimates needing calibration rather than universal truth.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Normative mechanics, security policy, modeling assumptions, implementation mechanisms, and empirical claims remain distinct.

evidence: All six sources were retrieved on 2026-09-02 and current guidance is attributed.
Snippet verification is required to reproduce deterministic cost computation before promotion.

Actual policy completeness, timing leakage, analyzer/executor agreement, predicted-versus-observed work, quotas, cancellation, cache isolation, federation trust, and manifest rollout remain deployment-specific evidence obligations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: No production graph, PDP, gateway/subgraph topology, operation corpus, quota service, or workload was empirically assessed.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed identity/policy separation, reachability-complete authorization, denial semantics, cache/federation/background boundaries, operation normalization, weighted cost, runtime containment, semantic quotas, trusted documents, introspection, and calibration as one layered model.

practitioner_review.notes: Checked implementability through immutable request identity, domain-owned policy APIs, request-scoped loaders, visibility predicates, normalized AST gates, coordinate weight metadata, cardinality caps, early admission, runtime counters/cancellation/bulkheads, work quotas, governed manifests, bounded tooling, telemetry, and matrix/fuzz/load tests.

pedagogical_review.notes: The module establishes authorization independently before demand control, develops structural and weighted models with explicit limits, and then composes lifecycle controls. Ten examples are distinct; five exercises progress from definitions/arithmetic to federated emergency coordination with complete answers.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
